title: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
summary: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the U.S. tightens its push to keep AI chips out of China

title: JWST studies a tiny, metal-poor galaxy with just a fraction of the sun's oxygen abundance
summary: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) have studied one of the most metal-poor galaxies known. Seen as it was around 12.2 billion years ago, LAP2 is a tiny system with a stellar mass comparable to that of a massive star cluster. The research paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Nov. 3.

title: Wave-like displays in animal groups may have evolved to deceive predators
summary: Some of the most striking patterns in collective behavior emerge in the face of danger. When a predator approaches, some animal groups morph into a vision of pulsing waves. These patterns might be more than a side effect of group living; they could have evolved as a form of deception, argue Dr. Eduardo Sampaio and professor Iain Couzin of the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior (MPI-AB) and the University of Konstanz in a Perspectives piece published in Science.

title: Runaway pulsar escapes the remnant of its own supernova
summary: A team of astronomers has spotted a rare example of a pulsar that has escaped the cloud of debris left by the supernova explosion in which it formed. Led by Rohit Dokara, formerly at the Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, the team made the discovery by chance, adding to just a handful of similar known cases.

title: 5G interference can alter high-impact weather forecasts
summary: Could leaks from future 5G networks interfere with satellite weather measurements and potentially alter forecasts? That's the concern of a group of researchers from the U.S. states of New Jersey and Maryland, with lead author Behzad Golparvar from Rutgers University in New Jersey.

title: Thailand tests find high lead, arsenic in river shellfish
summary: Thai authorities have found dangerous levels of arsenic and lead in shellfish and other species in rivers contaminated by suspected mining pollution from neighboring Myanmar, an official said Thursday.

title: Global maritime trade set for zero growth in 2026: UN
summary: Global maritime trade—which carries more than 80% of the world's goods—is set to stagnate in 2026 due to shipping disruptions and trade uncertainties arising from the war in the Middle East, the United Nations said Thursday.

title: Protein redesign boosts DNA insertion activity and reveals how molecular machinery selects targets
summary: Genome engineering is exciting, given its vast potential to treat and even cure diseases, but it is still a largely uncharted biomedical innovation. Scientists at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital recently uncovered the mechanisms involved in precisely integrating DNA into a target genomic location using CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs). By studying type I-F3 CAST, the researchers unveiled structural findings that explain how this CAST family achieves successful DNA integration at precise target sites and offer insights for future genomic engineering approaches. The results were published in Nature.

title: Do all groups drift toward rule by the few? Not when time is on their side
summary: For more than a century, a bleak idea has hung over the ideal of democracy: Given enough time, every group ends up ruled by a few. The idea, known as the iron law of oligarchy, was first proposed by the sociologist Robert Michels in the early 1900s.

title: Learning facts out of interest may take less mental effort than learning them for money
summary: When completing tasks or acquiring information, humans can be driven by intrinsic and extrinsic motivations. The term intrinsic motivation entails doing something because it is interesting to us or we find it enjoyable, while extrinsic motivation means doing it to obtain a reward, such as money, praise or a good grade.

title: Two mechanisms of amino acid transport in a rare disease-associated protein revealed
summary: Cells must constantly exchange amino acids with their environment to make proteins and support numerous bodily processes. To do this, they have specialized transporters located in their membranes.
